## What it is

- The **SG** is a "solid-body electric guitar model introduced by Gibson in 1961", as a successor to the Les Paul (Wikipedia, "Gibson SG").
- It has "a volume and a tone control for each individual pickup" and a three-way switch (Wikipedia).
- Scale 24.75 inches, like the Les Paul (Wikipedia). Its body is thinner, with two horns.

## Its sound

- The same circuit as the Les Paul: two humbuckers, each with its own volume and tone.
- Its neck joins the body further up, so the neck pickup is further from the bridge: nearer the string's middle (this page's estimate of the distance). It hears even fewer high harmonics: rounder.
- Bridge pickup: the bite of AC/DC and early Black Sabbath records (players named in Wikipedia).

Lemme, Helmuth E. W. "The Secrets of Electric Guitar Pickups." [buildyourguitar.com/resources/lemme/](https://buildyourguitar.com/resources/lemme/). Resonance of most pickups with a normal cable 2,000-5,000 Hz; inductance 1-10 H (not read directly: certificate expired 2026-11-26; unverified).

"Pickup (music technology)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickup_(music_technology)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickup_(music_technology)). Single coils pick up hum; humbucker coils cancel it; self-capacitance + cable resonate with the inductance; more turns, lower resonance.

Tillman, J. Donald. "Response Effects of Guitar Pickup Position and Width." 2000, updated 17 Oct. 2002. [www.till.com/articles/PickupResponse/index.html](https://www.till.com/articles/PickupResponse/index.html).
